correctness.rationale: For 1≤t<m≤n, each side has a vertex on the opposite side adjacent to all its vertices, forcing every nonempty side-color class to have odd size. For a marked a_i the witness b_i deletes just one occurrence of its color, so a marked class larger than one would become positive even. Properness allows a cross-shore color only on the two ends of a deleted pair. Conversely, these singleton deletions can only turn a count of one into zero, so the block-and-pair data are sufficient. With r,s unmatched blocks and j shared pairs there are 2t−j+r+s classes, and naming them gives the stated falling factorial. The minimum is at j=t and at one odd block on an odd-sized side or two on an even-sized side; in the latter case divide the 2^(w−1) odd subsets by two for complementation. At the full even crown endpoint, the bipartition coloring is strong odd since n−1 is odd and an edge forces two colors. The restored graph has u=v=1, giving n+1 colors and proving the jump, including n=2. The independent replay agrees with all profile coefficients on 87,448 partitions across 16 triples and tests explicit colorings on both actual graphs before and after restoration at 25 even sizes through n=50.
residual_risks: In the bundled edge-jump loop (verify.py lines 136–145), the restored graph's color count is checked by substituting in expected_chi, not by graph enumeration. Separate bundled construction tests include balanced sizes through 31. The independent replay tests explicit restorations through 50, not a lower-bound search at those larger sizes. The proof, not these finite checks, establishes the general lower bound.
